metas.name: Architecture - Røros Architecture
metas.note: The old mining town of Røros can be recognised by the densely built traditional wooden architecture.

metas.name: Architecture - White House Village
metas.note: While completely white wooden houses can be found in the entire country, they're especially common on the southern coast, where you'll commonly see entire villages made up of them.

metas.name: Coverage Meta - Snow Road
metas.note: The road between Atna and Ringebu in Innlandet is completely covered in snow. You will find a winter wonderland with green rocks
metas.footer: Source: Unique Roads of the World by Figsy

metas.name: Coverage Meta - Thick Snow Road
metas.note: This road between Aadneram and Nomeland in Agder features a thick 1m high snow along the skinny road. You will not find trees along this road.
metas.footer: Source: Unique Roads of the World by Figsy

metas.name: Infrastructure - Bamboo Snow Pole
metas.note: Bamboo snowpoles are regional and can mostly be found in Innlandet, Akershus, Østfold, Buskerud and Vestfold but can also be found rarely in Trøndelag, Vestland, Agder, Telemark and Rogaland.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Bergen Hydrant
metas.note: You can find this specific design of green fire hydrants in Bergen.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Big Wooden Snowpole
metas.note: Big wooden sticks are found on roads that are covered with snow almost the entire year. So far, they've been spotted on the road that runs north of Hardangervidda National Park, on the road west of Jotunheimen and southwest of Valdres Natur-og kulturpark.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Black Snow Poles
metas.note: Black plastic snowpoles are more regional and will mostly be found in Trøndelag, Møre og Romsdal and Vestland, but can also be found in Nordland and more rarely in Innlandet, Buskerud, Rogaland and Telemark

metas.name: Infrastructure - Oslo Pole Plate
metas.note: Fairly large black or red pole plates can be found in Oslo.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Rusty Guardrail
metas.note: Rusty guardrails are almost exclusively found in coastal regions, and particularly on the southern half of the west coast.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Senja Snowpoles
metas.note: Green plastic snowpoles are found mostly around the island of Senja in Troms since the company selling these is also located there. The company also sells other colors less frequently. These can also less commonly be found all over Troms and Finnmark.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Small Blue Snowpole
metas.note: Small blue snowpoles can be found around Elverum.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Two Red Stripes
metas.note: Two red stripes going around lamp posts are commonly found in Stavanger.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Wide Black ID
metas.note: Small, wide black pole plates, with a single line of letters and digits, can be found in southeastern Norway.

metas.name: Landscape - 82 (Andoya)
metas.note: The 82 on the island of Andoya, which is part of the Lofoten archipelago, is flat apart from one tabletop looking hill. In generall, the hills on this road are quite unique and recognizable. You will find short scrubs along the road. Often, you will be able to see water.
metas.footer: Source: Unique Roads of the World by Figsy

metas.name: Landscape - Atlanterhavsveien
metas.note:
This road uses dark rocks as bridges. You will see water on both sides of the road. The coverage features dark clouds.

The road includes the famous Storseisundet bridge.
metas.footer: Source: Unique Roads of the World by Figsy

metas.name: Landscape - Deep Fjords
metas.note: While fjords can be found along most of the Norwegian coast, deep fjords surrounded by tall mountains are most common between Bergen and Trondheim.

metas.name: Landscape - E10 in Lofoten
metas.note: This road features huge mountains. It is a skinny road that has water to the east. Lots of sections have bridges or open tunnels. You will frequently find fireweed on the sides of the road. The vegetation on this road has a yellowish tone.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/norway for more clues.

metas.name: Landscape - E10 on the border of Troms and Nordland
metas.note: This road runs through a valley. You can see a big mountain range along the road, with no trees on the mountain. Some sections are very green, and some section feature fireweed.
metas.footer: Source: Unique Roads of the World by Figsy

metas.name: Landscape - E10, East of Narvik
metas.note: This road is very green and usually features big mountains with no trees. Right on the Swedish border you will find parts without trees.
metas.footer: Source: Unique Roads of the World by Figsy

metas.name: Landscape - End of the World Road
metas.note: This famous road can be identified by the lack of trees and the small white rocks. The visibility in the coverage is somewhat low. Some sections are very flat, while others can have small hills and lakes.
metas.footer: Source: Unique Roads of the World by Figsy

metas.name: Landscape - Exposed Rock
metas.note: Exposed rock, often spotted with small coastal pines and bushes, is mainly found on the south coast.

metas.name: Landscape - Highlands
metas.note: Barren highlands, with no trees or bushes, and often with rocky mountains along the road, are mostly found in the southwest.

metas.name: Landscape - Lofoten Mountains
metas.note: Distinct, sharp, rocky mountains with few trees can be seen on the Lofoten Archipelago.

metas.name: Landscape - Lysevegen
metas.note: Lysevegen is a very windy and skinny road with 28 180° turns down the mountain. Notably, there are big power lines visible. You can see huge mountains in the distance. The coverage is very cloudy.
metas.footer: Source: Unique Roads of the World by Figsy

metas.name: Landscape - Northeastern Landscape
metas.note: The northeast of Norway can typically be recognized by a somewhat rolling landscape, rather than tall mountains, and vegetation mainly consisting of very small birches combined with patched grass.

metas.name: Landscape - Northern Coastal Grasslands
metas.note: Coastal grasslands with little to no other vegetation and only somewhat low, distant mountains can be found by coastal roads in the far north.

metas.name: Landscape - Oslo Farmlands
metas.note: The largest concentration of farmland is found in the southeast, in the general vicinity of Oslo. The area is much flatter than most of the country, and it is common to get a rolling landscape with smooth, round forested hills in the distance. The area southeast of Oslo is particularly flat.

metas.name: Landscape - Røst Island
metas.note: This island has only Gen 2 coverage. You will see lots of boats everywhere. The landscape is flat and islandish (duh).
metas.footer: Source: Unique Roads of the World by Figsy

metas.name: Landscape - Russian Border Road
metas.note: Along the Russian border you can see this noticeably humid and green-looking road, with very overcast and occasionally foggy coverage. The trees are somewhat low and mainly consist of thin birches and pines.

metas.name: Landscape - Stavanger Farmlands
metas.note: The farmland south of Stavanger is flatter than most of the country. The fields look vast and open, and it is very common to see rock walls made of large, round rocks. Furthermore, rather than crops, most fields will only contain grass.

metas.name: Landscape - Trollstigen
metas.note: Trollstigen leads down a huge mountain, and is surrounded by such. The road is very steep and windy. The rock is very dark and has green moss on it. Some sections are cut into the rock, with waterfalls appearing.
metas.footer: Source: Unique Roads of the World by Figsy

metas.name: Landscape - Trondheim Farmlands
metas.note: The farmlands surrounding Trondheim are generally very hilly, and the hills are typically both steeper and more uneven than in the southeast.

metas.name: Language - Russian language
metas.note: Russian can sometimes be seen alongside Norwegian on signs near the Russian border. It is mostly found on roads E6 and E105 near Kirkenes.

metas.name: Language - Sámi Signs
metas.note: Bilingual signs with Sámi can be found in several northern areas in Norway. While the Sámi languages are very different from Norwegian, the best way to recognize them are the letters Á, Đ and the use of several vowels in a row, something which is uncommon in Norwegian. Note that not all signs in these areas will be bilingual.

metas.name: Vegetation - Bracken
metas.note: This species of fern (Pteridium aquilinum, also known as bracken) which typically has a fairly tall stem and many wide leafs branching out, is mostly found in the south of Norway. Beware that other species of ferns can be found further north.

metas.name: Vegetation - Bright Moss
metas.note: Brightly colored moss is common to find in the area between Lillehammer and Oppdal

metas.name: Vegetation - Maple
metas.note: Maples are mainly found in the south, particularly by the farmlands around Oslo.

metas.name: Vegetation - Oaks
metas.note: Oaks are mainly found in the far south of Norway.

metas.name: Vegetation - Pine
metas.note: Pines are most common in coastal and far inland areas in the southern half of the country.

metas.name: Vegetation - Spruce
metas.note: Spruces are mainly found in the southern half of the country, particularly in the southeast and around Trondheim.
